short: Microstructural and mechanical anisotropy of selective laser
title: Microstructural and mechanical anisotropy of selective laser melted IN718 superalloy at room and high temperatures using small punch test

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Mechanisms behind the orientation dependence (anisotropy) of SLM IN718 mechanical properties have not been discussed in detail. Use small punch testing (hemispherical punch bulging a 500 um disc, load-displacement recorded) to assess anisotropy.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (DES/method), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/forming)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Grains are columnar along BD, spanning several layers, in side sections and near-equiaxed in top sections. Strong cube-type <100> texture with <100> parallel to BD in both top and side material.
states.detail: Absorbed: n7 (STR/microstructure/shape), n8 (STR/microstructure/orientation), n9 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n11 (STR/defect/extended). Premises: Nb segregation during SLM solidification of IN718 forms intercellular Nb-rich Laves and gamma'' particles; With 30 um layers a side disc (8.7 mm span along BD) crosses ~290 layers, a top disc (500 um thick) ~17 layers

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Side-disc columnar grains lie across the load, rotate during bulging and put slip systems near 45 deg (high Schmid factor), raising dislocation multiplication and work hardening; top-disc grains stay parallel to load (low Schmid factor). At 650 C the side disc loses strength by dynamic recovery of its high SLM-induced dislocation density; the low-dislocation top disc does not.
states.detail: Absorbed: m1 (MEC/pathway), m2 (MEC/pathway), m3 (MEC/pathway), p2 (PRP/value), p1 (PRP/value), p3 (PRP/behavior_class), p4 (PRP/value), p5 (PRP/behavior_class). Premises: Schmid factor is maximal when slip plane and slip direction both lie at 45 deg to the load; At high temperature dislocations move under a lower applied force; At high temperature grain boundaries become weaker than grain interiors; A ductile SPT load-displacement curve divides into zones I-VI: elastic bending, plastic bending, membrane stretching, necking/crack initiation, crack growth, fracture

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The better loading orientation switches with temperature: side discs are superior at RT, top discs match or slightly exceed them at 650 C

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: SLM IN718 is mechanically anisotropic in SPT, with an orientation ranking that reverses at 650 C, attributed to columnar grain orientation vs load, residual stress and Laves/grain-boundary weakening

nodes.title: MICRO, F3
nodes.head: 3D OM block: side faces show BD-elongated columnar grains crossing several melt-pool layers; top face shows melt tracks with smaller irregular grains
nodes.solves: Grains are columnar along BD, spanning several layers, in side sections and near-equiaxed in top sections
nodes.note: text: columns 50-250 um long, 12-35 um wide, 4-12 layers
nodes.necessity_reason: n7 keeps shown support from o3 after removal.

nodes.title: SEM, F4
nodes.head: SEM/ECCI: bright 'Laves' particles sit discretely at cell junctions in the top section; in the side section they form a 'Chain of Laves' along BD-parallel cell walls
nodes.solves: Intercellular Laves particles are discrete in the top section but form continuous chains along BD-parallel cell walls in the side section
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n9 (o8).

nodes.title: PROCESS, XRD, F5
nodes.head: XRD: (200) is the strongest reflection (~2x (111)) in both SLM sections, whereas the powder pattern is (111)-dominated with weak (200)
nodes.solves: Strong cube-type <100> texture with <100> parallel to BD in both top and side material
nodes.note: text/Table 2: texture parameter TP(200) = 3.2 top, 3.0 side
nodes.necessity_reason: n8 keeps shown support from o6, o7 after removal.

nodes.title: EBSD, XRD:poleFigure, F5, F6
nodes.head: XRD (100) pole figures of side and top sections each show one strong central maximum (Max 5.94 and 5.26). EBSD {100} pole figures of both sections show maxima at the centre and at the X and Y rims (cube component), texture index 2.45 side and 2.56 top
nodes.solves: Strong cube-type <100> texture with <100> parallel to BD in both top and side material
nodes.note: the legend of F5b sits inside the F5c crop (both legends appear in F5c) max 4.06 side, 3.49 top
nodes.detail: o6: XRD (100) pole figures of side and top sections each show one strong central maximum (Max 5.94 and 5.26); o7: EBSD {100} pole figures of both sections show maxima at the centre and at the X and Y rims (cube component), texture index 2.45 side and 2.56 top

nodes.title: MICRO, F9
nodes.head: RT fracture: side surface is rough with fine cup-like relief; top surface shows smooth flat facets with steps and little deformation. 650 C side fracture: a 'Crack' along a boundary and tall faceted relief shaped like 'Columnar grains'
nodes.solves: At RT the side disc fractures in a ductile, fine-featured (dimpled) mode and the top disc by flat brittle facets
nodes.note: at 2000x (F9b) dimples are not clearly resolved; the ductile reading is weaker than the text states strings written on F9e/F9f; F9 has no panels offered, so no packet annotation list exists
nodes.necessity_reason: p3, p5 keeps shown support from o17 after removal.

nodes.title: XRD:poleFigure, F6
nodes.head: Side and top {100} pole figures show the same cube pattern in their own disc frames, so the disc-normal (punch) axis is a <100> direction for both specimens
nodes.solves: Side-disc columnar grains lie across the load, rotate during bulging and put slip systems near 45 deg (high Schmid factor), raising dislocation multiplication and work hardening; top-disc grains stay parallel to load (low Schmid factor)
nodes.note: with cube texture the initial crystallographic loading axis is equivalent for top and side discs; the Schmid-factor difference in m1 therefore rests on grain rotation/morphology, not on initial crystal orientation
nodes.detail: a1: Side and top {100} pole figures show the same cube pattern in their own disc frames, so the disc-normal (punch) axis is a <100> direction for both specimens
nodes.inner_audit: a1: with cube texture the initial crystallographic loading axis is equivalent for top and side discs; the Schmid-factor difference in m1 therefore rests on grain rotation/morphology, not on initial crystal orientation
